bootstrap.usable_step: k64 + b84: first lstat of both roots; settle to mount-1 end + 40 s, READY still last; baseline OBSERVE with no open provider claim; final lstat; claims OBSERVE every 5 s for at most 30 s until each provider shows a TERMINAL GETATTR and PROCESS_EXIT numbered after the baseline; at most about 100 s after mount-1; summary ready only if it passes. zq3-r10 and zq3-r11 passed it (L = 2); with 1a4 a probe behind a view stuck in a recall fails ETIMEDOUT after 30 s (a finding)

candidate.daemon_changes: y94: an early DRAINED (sent while an all-domain recall still waits for a peer's INSTALLED_DRAIN) is answered BLOCKED, not STALE, if the guest's own INSTALLED_DRAIN of that recall is archived; the BLOCKED bound follows still-blocked peers; on top of b94 (194), r84 and l84
candidate.expectations: R11-1: an early DRAINED is answered BLOCKED and accepted once the peer's INSTALLED_DRAIN arrives, so an all-domain recall completes and T1-T4 should pass; R11-2 (guest side): a syscall stuck behind a wedged recall fails ETIMEDOUT after 30 s instead of hanging. Known risks not fixed: z94 (a read-only root OPEN under the caller's own observation lease self-conflicts and starts an all-domain recall; expect such recalls, now survivable) and 0a4 (the host never drops a participant that stops acknowledging). Any ETIMEDOUT, 'view control worker stopped' line or 'initial attributes timed out behind a recall' line is a finding
